So, since folks seemed to have shown and interest in all this I figured you might be interested in some more granular info. (warning: wall-o-text incoming)

So to follow up on the original post…. I was getting very disillusioned with the corporate and city “rat race” mentality. The software company I was working for kinda went evil with no regard for customer satisfaction, then getting in bed majorly with the idea of the corporate/state surveillance and the over watch umbrella, coupled with just ugly internal politics for the sake of having arbitrary “power over some internal group” that took up about half the working day… It made me…. disillusioned….

…and city living. After having done it for over 15 years. It seemed to boil down and be nothing more then…. Go to the movies, shop and consume, go to the new hip restaurant, go see some semi-bad band play live in a club somewhere, go get drunk in a bar… shop, maybe go to the museum again and again and again, shop, drive maniacally to go shop. the work 10 hours a day, just to afford all that... Lots of folks seemed to “have to be entertained constantly” and could not allow themselves any quite time…if you will With the occasional outlier of having some friend go on a trip, or personally taking a trip, or publish a book or play in their band somewhere. Basically another “social interaction” with a relatively small group of folks type of thing and just rush, rush, rush everywhere.….… Rinse and repeat. It seemed to get stale.

Oh did I mention the two hour commute of only 8 miles, one way, to get from where I lived, to where I worked, for a total of about four-five hours a day sitting in a car or on mass transit? And then the general hostility that almost everyone extruded through-out the day? (which you can even see and sense in some of the replies that folks have posted here)

Also of note, when I originally moved to the city I remember how clean the skys were. When I moved out I marveled at how brown and dirty the air was, almost like a factory city in china. Cities are highly polluted places and you don’t even notice it there…. The boiling frog phenomenon and all that….

So I decided to try something different. I sold my house and bought five acres on the top of a mountain that had a small (700 sq foot) house that need a lot of work. Moved and got to work.

Since I had lots of city living experience and not a lot of woods living, there was a transition of about a year or so, where I “came down” from the adrenaline rush/fatigue of the city life (you don’t realized how jacked up you constantly are, living in a city, until you are out of it…) and got into the groove of living a slower paced life and learned wood skills. I fixed up the house and started to go off grid with it. Solar and wind power for the lights and such. Built a 200 sqft wood fired bath house with a shower and a sauna (that only cost 800.00 usd n total) since my main water tends to freeze up in the dead of the winter its nice to still have a sauna and a shower…. I run on 100% wood heat so I have to cut firewoord every year. Started gardening and just generally relaxed a bit. I have super clear skys at night so I took up astronomy with a cheap ebay telescope and live near a beautiful lake, so bought an old sailboat and taught myself how to sail.

I have a well for water and a septic system, so I don’t have to pay any water /sewer/garbage bills each month and get about ¾ of my power from solar and wind (witch cost me about 4k to set up) so I only have about a 10.00 a month electric bill and my dial up phone and dial up cost is about 60.00 a month.. So food and the car ops (I own an old beater that is paid for) and Inet are my only real bills and I really don’t drive the car that much. anymore…. So my cost of living is fairly small.(except for yearly property taxes) I do have to police my own garbage and make a garbage run to the local transfer point about once a week and that cost is figured into my local taxes .
I’m in totally better shape then I ever have been and much more relaxed. I Mt bike and hike every day and in the winter x-country ski every where, from just off my front porch… I’ve learned to cook and am fairly good at it now, since there are no fast food places anywhere. And still can go get drunk in the local bar and eat in the restaurants when I want. I can still go the the local museums and go shop, still play vids with friends (although not so much onlining with the low bandwidth) and all that city stuff that I usta do, if I want.

What do I do for healthcare, some asked. Easy, I haven’t dropped out and live a totally secluded life, contrary to some of the assumptions made by responders, life does go on with goods and services outside of major urban settings. Dropping completely out…. That just seems unreasonable. There are lots of doctors in the closest town (about 70 miles away) and there is a “hartflight” helicopter that you can sign up for, for like 90.00 a year in case you get in some sort of catastrophic emergency. They will fly you into the nearest hospital in minutes. There is a local volunteer ambulance service here and I joined the local volunteer fire department, since it’s a really small community and everyone has to pull a little weight to make it work for everyone else. There is even an old veterinarian who drinks down at the local bar, who will dispense some first aid and antibiotics for those in need for a few drinks in return.

What do I do for money? Again, life just doesn’t end outside of a city limit. I do a fair amount of remote web dev work. I help the locals with tech support on their comps and I have taken up virtual reality development. ( I even mod the voat virtualreality sub) I taught myself unity and am weeks away from releasing my first VR game. (heres my bad website on the game if anyone is interested…. http://huesgfx.com/firedrake and some other VR projects I have done. Http://huesgfx.com/vr/vrmain.html)) I make significantly less then I did in a city, but then my expenses are significantly less here so it all kind of works out. Once you get comfortable with the idea the money is not the end all, be all, life tends to balance out. I should note, that I also never wracked up any debt. I always paid for things with cash or saved up till I could. (with the exception of course of my house) So, I don’t have the debt slave yoke around my neck, which probably made this move to the woods, much easier.)

One huge kicker for me is Inet access. ( I also don’t get TV signal or barely any radio) People take it for granted in the city, (I sure did) but anywhere outside of a city it’s a real bitch to get. I ended up having to multiplex two old dial up lines together with two modems and windows XP to get a 100k connection. One a good day it runs about 80k but sometimes gets up to 100k. It’s slow, but it works. There are no cable nodes or DLS here. Cell (3g) is spotty at best. So it is what it is….

On a side note. Just a 1/2 mile from my house is one of the fastest fiber optic networks in the land. But it is owned by DHS and used to monitor the Canadian border for whatever reason. And no one can get access…. My tax dollars at work!

One interesting thing I was not prepared for. Is everyone is armed here. There are lots of guns and everyone has a pistol on them or a rifle close by in the truck. The police after literally about an hour to hour and a half away if you need them. We live in bear country, both Grizzly and black bears and always have bear trouble in the summers (the blacks and cinnamon bears are the worst.. grizzlies tend to keep to themselves and rarely cause troubles, but sometimes). We also have the wolfs and contrary to inet beliefs, these things are trouble and I’ve heard of an attack or two a year on people, usually in the winters…. And folks tend to come up in the woods and drop off their pitbulls from the city thinking they would “rather give their dogs a chance, instead of putting them down or putting them in shelters” so we have a breed of wild pitbulls that are getting in with the coyotes and wolf packs and are MAJOR trouble. We also get the occasional lion that can cause some trouble. (had three in the valley last year that ate everyone’s dogs and cats and livestocks all summer and may or may not have been stalking the neighbors small children…. Details and game cam photos are a tad sketchy there…) And we do get the occasional meth fiends and general wackos that seem to think that they can come here and cause havoc, stealing and such. So everyone carries a gun and I have learned that an armed society, tends to be a polite society…. Anyway,

Some details for ya…. Life is what you make it, whether you live in a downtown city or off on a mountain top. Only you can be the judge of what’s best for you.

For Saturday morning, I fix my favorite breakfast: biscuits and gravy. Since it's my cheat day, and the missus doesn't eat red meat, there's almost always leftovers that I don't want to go bad. I've tried freezing gravy in the past, and it turns out poorly (loses all consistency). Last week, I tried thickening with cornstarch instead of using a roux, and it turned out perfectly! Still had that awesome gravy thickness, and the flavor was untouched. Since biscuits are best fresh, I bake mine every week, as well. Recipe is as follows for two drop style biscuits:

1/2 cup flour

1/2 tsp baking powder

1/2 tsp sugar

1/4 tsp salt

1 1/2 tbsp cold butter

1/4 cup milk (evaporated milk is fine, haven't tried with almond milk)

Mix dry ingredients. Cube cold butter and mix in by hand (you can use a dough cutter, I just don't like dirtying more than I need to). Mix in milk. Drop onto baking pan and bake at 400° for 12-14 minutes.
